narratives.name: AI-Ready Enterprise Play Context and Rationale
narratives.description: Why the AI-Ready Enterprise Play alpha matters within the sales play framework.

narrativeContexts.context: Enterprise customers face a critical gap between AI proof-of-concept success and production AI deployment at scale, driven by infrastructure fragmentation across disconnected tools, spiraling GPU costs, and inconsistent security posture across AI workloads.

The AI-Ready Enterprise play equips sellers to position Red Hat's open hybrid AI platform as the trusted foundation for production AI, orchestrating four TDPs (Server/Cloud OS, App Platform, Automation, AI Platform) into a coherent infrastructure stack that addresses cost, complexity, and choice concerns.

Sellers apply the Customer Lens to assess AI maturity, engage CIO/CTO/VP Infrastructure personas with tailored discovery frameworks, align the four-TDP AI stack to the customer's technology decisions, and articulate value through quantified business impact evidence from reference deployments.

Customers achieve a clear path from AI proof-of-concept to production, with reduced GPU infrastructure costs, simplified multi-environment AI operations, and freedom from proprietary AI platform lock-in through Red Hat's open-source approach.

narratives.name: AI-Ready Enterprise Practice Intent
narratives.description: The end-to-end narrative of the AI-Ready Enterprise play from market discovery through deal advancement and expansion.

narrativeContexts.context: Enterprise customers struggle to move AI initiatives beyond proof-of-concept due to infrastructure fragmentation, spiraling GPU costs, security concerns across AI workloads, and skills gaps in production AI operations.

The AI-Ready Enterprise play structures Red Hat's AI positioning around three value drivers -- Cost (reduce infrastructure and GPU expenses through consolidation), Complexity (simplify AI deployment with a unified platform across hybrid environments), and Choice (avoid vendor lock-in with an open-source AI stack) -- validated through customer reference evidence from production AI deployments.

The play orchestrates four TDPs (Server/Cloud OS, App Platform, Automation, AI Platform) into a coherent AI infrastructure stack narrative, enabling sellers to present an integrated solution from infrastructure foundation through AI model serving.

Sellers engage CIO/VP Digital Transformation, CTO/Head of AI/ML, and VP/Dir of Infrastructure personas with persona-tailored discovery questions and value propositions, building multi-stakeholder alignment around production AI infrastructure investment.

Technical validation through AI workload demonstrations and proof-of-value exercises confirms platform fit, with competitive differentiation defended against proprietary AI platforms and cloud-native alternatives.

AI infrastructure deployments expand as organizations scale from pilot AI workloads to enterprise-wide production AI, with subscription growth driven by increasing GPU node count, model deployment volume, and automation scope.

narratives.name: Applying the AI Customer Lens
narratives.description: How to systematically assess a customer's AI maturity and infrastructure pain using the AI-Ready Enterprise Customer Lens.

narrativeContexts.context: Enterprise customers evaluating AI infrastructure investments face a complex landscape of disconnected AI tools, GPU cost management challenges, and uncertainty about production readiness.

Apply the AI-Ready Enterprise Customer Lens to systematically assess the customer's AI maturity (POC, pilot, scaling, production), identify specific pain points, and map desired outcomes to the play's structured framework.

Review the play's pain taxonomy covering infrastructure fragmentation, security concerns, skills gaps, and cost escalation, then validate which pains resonate with the customer's specific AI situation using discovery questions.

narrativeContexts.context: AI infrastructure decisions involve multiple stakeholders with distinct priorities -- CIOs balancing AI investment with IT operations, CTOs evaluating infrastructure readiness for production AI, and infrastructure VPs managing modernization demands.
Engage each AI persona using the play's structured profiles that define what they care about, their current reality, the impacts they face, tailored discovery questions, and what wins them over.

narratives.name: Aligning the Four-TDP AI Stack
narratives.description: How to construct a layered AI infrastructure solution narrative from the four TDPs powering the AI-Ready Enterprise play.

narrativeContexts.context: AI infrastructure requires multiple technology layers working together -- from the operating system foundation through application runtime to automation and AI platform services -- but customers often evaluate these in isolation.

Align the four TDPs powering the AI-Ready Enterprise play to the customer's specific technology decision landscape, constructing a layered solution narrative that presents an integrated AI infrastructure stack.

Connect Server/Cloud OS (infrastructure foundation optimized for AI workloads) to App Platform (AI application runtime and Kubernetes for AI) to Automation (operational AI and automated infrastructure management) to AI Platform (model serving, training, and inference), with each layer addressing specific customer technology decisions.
Customer sees a coherent AI infrastructure architecture rather than four separate products, with each TDP addressing a specific layer of their AI deployment requirements.

narrativeContexts.context: AI infrastructure investments compete for budget with many priorities, and customers need quantified business justification beyond technology capability claims to secure funding.
